subject: Re: KyberCorp RFP - Key escrow, rotation and BYOK controls
messages:
From: James Wen <james.wen@kybercorp.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Security Team <security@kybercorp.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: KyberCorp RFP - Key Escrow & Rotation Questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking the time to engage with KyberCorp on this RFP. Our security and cloud teams have a handful of detailed questions around your encryption and key management model — specifically: BYOK flows, escrow policies, rotation cadence and cross-region key handling for multi-tenant deployments.

Can you provide a written response to the attached questionnaire (we've highlighted our must-haves) and a diagram showing where customer keys are stored and how Redwood interacts with HSMs/KMS? Also:
- Will Redwood accept customer-managed keys in AWS, GCP, and Azure HSMs?
- Do you support key import (BYOK) and wrap/unwrap operations with customer-held keys?
- Describe your rotation policy and whether automatic or customer-initiated rotations are supported.
- Are there any circumstances where Redwood would perform key escrow or require access to raw key material?

Attached: kyber_kms_questions_v1.xlsx (questionnaire)

We are aiming to evaluate vendors by 10/10 and would appreciate an initial response by 10/02 so we can schedule a technical follow-up.

Best,
James Wen
Senior Cloud Security Manager
KyberCorp
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: James Wen <james.wen@kybercorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KyberCorp RFP - Key Escrow & Rotation Questions

James —

Thanks for the clear list. We're attaching a consolidated response and a network/crypto diagram that shows where keys are provisioned, stored, and how we route wrap/unwrap calls to customer KMS/HSM. High-level answers up front:

- BYOK: Supported across AWS KMS (Import Key Material and External Key Store), GCP Cloud KMS (external key support), and Azure Key Vault / HSM. We support both import (customer uploads key material) and external key references (we call customer-managed key endpoints).
- Wrap/Unwrap: We perform wrap/unwrap operations only via the customer's KMS endpoint. Redwood never persists unencrypted raw key material.
- Rotation: Rotation can be automatic (policy-driven on a per-tenant basis) or manual (customer-initiated via API). We support scheduled rotations, key versioning, and a configurable grace period for replay/rollback windows.
- Escrow: Redwood does not escrow customer master keys. In exceptional operational scenarios (disaster recovery where a customer has explicitly agreed to an escrow in contract), we will follow an auditable, contract-backed escrow workflow that requires multi-party approval and HSM-backed sealed storage.

Attachments: Redwood_KMS_Response_v1.pdf; Redwood-BYO-KMS-Diagram.png

I pulled Priyom in to confirm the HSM operational controls and Monica to surface any procurement/contract implications. We'll be available for a technical call.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Product, Security and Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KyberCorp RFP - Key Escrow & Rotation Questions

Quick internal notes (looping here so Markus can include clarifications in the bundle):

Markus — a few operational clarifications we should surface explicitly in the response:

1) HSM models / attestation: we currently integrate with AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM and partner with several on-prem HSM vendors (Thales, Utimaco) via PKCS#11 endpoints. We should include our attestation procedure (HSM firmware versions, FIPS 140-2/3 statuses, and how customers can request device cert chains).

2) Key import vs. external reference: clarify that when customers import key material (BYOK import), we never export the plaintext again — we use KMS APIs for crypto ops. For external key references (e.g., AWS EKM), we route requests over mutually authenticated TLS with client certs.

3) Rotation window and compatibility: recommend surfacing default rotation cadence (90 days for ephemeral DEKs, 365 days for CMKs unless customer overrides). Mention explicit backward-compatibility policy: decryption of historical ciphertext is possible for N months (configurable per contract) while key versions are retained.

4) Escrow edge-case: we need to provide the exact escrow runbook steps (approval gate, dual-sig, sealed envelope in HSM) — Priyom offered to redact sensitive operational specifics but give enough evidence for Kyber's compliance team.

Monica — can you confirm whether procurement will accept the escrow language that requires a notarized contract amendment? If not, we'll propose an alternative: emergency key-swap SLA and on-prem key transfer process.

—Priyom
Senior Applied Cryptography Engineer
From: James Wen <james.wen@kybercorp.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Security Team <security@kybercorp.com>, Procurement <procurement@kybercorp.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2026 17:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KyberCorp RFP - Key Escrow & Rotation Questions

Markus, Monica, Priyom —

Appreciate the thorough packet. The Kyber security review had two follow-ups: a request for the HSM attestation cert chain (we'd prefer device certs for the HSM you referenced) and a suggested edit to escrow language: they want escrow only via an independent escrow agent and with a defined retrieval process.

Next steps: can Redwood provide the redacted escrow runbook and the attestation cert bundle by EOB 10/09? If possible, please include an explicit API snippet showing how Redwood calls an external KMS (mutual-TLS handshake + sample curl showing client cert). We'll schedule the technical deep-dive for 10/12 (tentative).

Also listed below are the attachments we've received from Redwood for the record: Redwood_KMS_Response_v1.pdf; Redwood-BYO-KMS-Diagram.png. Please send the additional items as separate attachments.

Thanks — talk soon.

James Wen
Senior Cloud Security Manager
KyberCorp
